title: Not good to be alone (Genesis 2:18–25)
hookLine: the only thing in creation God calls not good is loneliness
carry: bone of my bones, flesh of my flesh

cards: Count the verdicts so far. Light: good. Dry land and sea: good.
Plants: good. Sun, moon and stars: good. Fish and birds, cattle and creeping things: good.
Everything together: very good. Genesis keeps saying it like a bell. Then, in the garden, with the first human freshly made and a whole world to tend, the bell rings wrong.
God looks at the man and says something is not good. Not sin. No serpent, no fruit, nothing has gone wrong yet.

teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a help like unto himself." The first thing in the Bible called not good isn't evil. It's being alone.
The man has God, a garden and work, and still something is missing. Then the word help. In Hebrew it's ezer kenegdo, a helper corresponding to him, one who stands facing him.

teach.h: EZER: A HELP, LIKE GOD IS.
teach.b: Ezer is not a servant's word: the Hebrew Bible uses it most often for God, who is Israel's help. So the help God promises isn't an assistant. It's a partner, an equal, someone who can look back.
God brings the animals to the man, and he names every one, cattle, birds, beasts of the field, but none of them is the help like himself.
So God casts the man into a deep sleep, takes one of his ribs, closes up the flesh, and builds a woman.
When he wakes and sees her, the first human words in the Bible spill out, close to a song: this now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh.
The Catechism says man and woman are made for each other, a communion of persons, and that this is where marriage begins.

teach.h: IT IS NOT GOOD FOR MAN TO BE ALONE.
teach.b: But the Church also reads the line more widely: no human being is made to be alone. Friendship, family, parish, neighbors: all of them answer the same not good. And the scene ends quietly.
They were both naked, and were not ashamed.

how: Genesis 2:18–24 is one of the Old Testament readings Catholic couples can choose for their wedding Mass, and the Church reads it as the beginning of marriage and of all human community.

games.q: you're the first human. God brings every animal before you, and you name them one by one. what do you find?
o: no help like yourself among them.
games.why: none of them is the help like himself. then God casts him into a deep sleep and builds the woman, and he wakes singing bone of my bones.

practice: Let one face come to mind: someone living by themselves, a widower down the street, a friend who moved to a new city, a coworker who eats lunch at the desk, an older relative whose phone doesn't ring much.
Picture where they are right now, what the room sounds like, and stay with that one person. If you pray, hold them before God by name.

wordCard.voice: Ezer kenegdo, the Hebrew for a help corresponding to him, an equal who can stand facing you: God's answer to the first not good. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a help corresponding to him, standing facing him. ezer is often used of God.

carryVoice: Your line: bone of my bones, flesh of my flesh. The first not good, and the first human words. Day three hundred thirty-seven.
